# Changelog

## 0.4.0

### New rule: `require-is-valid-call-check`

- Flags methods whose JSDoc documents `DisconnectedError`
  (`AsyncPlayerJoinBeforeEvent.allowJoin`, `disallowJoin`, `disconnect`, and
  any later callback method with the same throw) unless `receiver.isValid()`
  was called in the same synchronous scope.
- The proof is a call. A property read of `isValid` does not count.
- Proofs clear after `await` / `yield` and do not cross deferred callbacks
  (`system.run`, `system.runTimeout`). Sync array callbacks inherit them.
- Recommended config enables the rule as `error`. Default modules are
  `@minecraft/server` and `@minecraft/server-admin`.

## 0.2.1

### Entity queries are no longer branded `Valid*`

- `world.getEntity`, `Dimension.getEntities`, and
  `Dimension.getEntitiesAtBlockLocation` now return plain `Entity` references
  in `valid-types.d.ts`. Query results are routinely stored past the tick or
  iterated by sweeps that remove entities mid-loop (a removed mount takes its
  riders with it), so a brand taken at query time was unsound for the dominant
  usage patterns — production Sentry data showed `InvalidEntityError` throws
  from exactly these paths.
- `require-is-valid-check` therefore now requires an `isValid` check before
  non-safe use of any entity obtained from those APIs, and
  `no-unnecessary-is-valid-check` no longer flags such checks as redundant.
- Player queries (`world.getAllPlayers`, `world.getPlayers`,
  `Dimension.getPlayers`) stay branded: script code does not despawn players
  mid-loop, and a player leaving invalidates at tick boundaries.

## 0.2.0

### New rule: `require-execution-privilege`

- Statically detects Bedrock execution-privilege violations (runtime
  `ReferenceError: Native function [...] cannot be used in restricted
execution.`) by trusting the privilege marker sentences in the installed
  `@minecraft/server` JSDoc (both the current `restricted-execution` and the
  legacy `read-only mode` wording).
- Flags forbidden calls and property edits in **restricted** contexts
  (before-event / custom-command callbacks) and non-allowlisted calls and
  property reads in **early** contexts (module top level, `startup`, top-level
  promise continuations). Escape semantics: `system.run*` always escapes to
  default; `await` escapes restricted but **not** early.
- Early property-read checks apply only to **class members** (native getters);
  enum members, interface properties (e.g. `Vector3.x`), and module-level
  consts are exempt.
- **Same-file synchronous call-graph propagation**: a restricted/early call to
  a same-file helper is scanned transitively (cycle-guarded, depth-capped) and
  violations are reported at the helper call site, naming both the helper and
  the offending API. Cross-file helpers remain out of scope.
- Enabled as `error` in the recommended config.

### `valid-types`

- Stop branding entity-subject after-event payloads. After-events dispatch at
  the end of the tick, so any entity that is the _subject_ of the event may
  already have been removed when the handler runs (e.g. killed and despawned
  by script in the same tick — the exact failure observed in production with
  `entityHitEntity.hitEntity.getComponent('health')` throwing
  `InvalidEntityError`). Removed `ValidEventCallback` subscribe overloads for:
  `dataDrivenEntityTrigger`, `effectAdd`, `entityDie`, `entityHeal`,
  `entityHealthChanged`, `entityHitBlock`, `entityHitEntity`, `entityHurt`,
  `entityItemDrop`, `entityItemPickup`, `entityStartSneaking`,
  `entityUpgrade`, `entityContainerClosed`, `entityContainerOpened`,
  `explosion`, `blockExplode`, `buttonPush`, `pressurePlatePop`,
  `pressurePlatePush`, `tripWireTrip`, `targetBlockHit`,
  `projectileHitBlock`, `projectileHitEntity`, and
  `playerInteractWithEntity` (after).
- `ProjectileHitEntityAfterEvent.getEntityHit()` no longer returns a branded
  entity (the hit entity may have died before after-event dispatch).
- Before-events stay branded (they run synchronously while the payload is
  alive), as do after-events whose payload is only the _acting_ player
  (`itemUse.source`, `playerBreakBlock.player`, `chatSend.sender`, …).

### Tests

- Rule-test fixtures no longer accidentally merge the shipped
  `valid-types.d.ts` into the rule-test program (`tests/fixtures/tsconfig.json`
  now excludes `valid-types-stub`, which is compiled as its own program).
- Cover plain entity-subject after-event payloads requiring `isValid`, and
  the compile fixture asserts hit/interact/projectile payloads are unbranded.

### Upgrade notes

Handlers for the events listed above must now guard with `entity.isValid`
(or an equivalent type-guard) before any non-safe use, exactly like
`entitySpawn` / `entityLoad` since 0.1.4.

## 0.1.4

### `valid-types`

- Keep `entitySpawn` and `entityLoad` payload entities unbranded. Earlier
  subscribers can remove the entity before later subscribers receive the same
  event, so those handlers must check `entity.isValid`.

### Tests / docs

- Cover `entitySpawn` / `entityLoad` requiring `isValid` before unsafe use,
  and allowing safe property reads (`id` / `typeId`) without a guard.
- Document the unbranded spawn/load contract in `require-is-valid-check` docs.

### Upgrade notes

After bumping, add `if (!entity.isValid) return;` (or equivalent) at the top of
`entitySpawn` / `entityLoad` handlers before any non-safe use. Remove any
assumption that those event payloads are already `ValidEntity`.

## 0.1.3

### `valid-types`

- Brand `Player.onScreenDisplay` as `ValidScreenDisplay`. A live player's screen
  display is a fresh handle (same contract as `Entity.getComponent`) — callers
  no longer need a second `display.isValid` check immediately after reading it.

### `require-is-valid-check` / brand detection

- Nested Valid\* members on **tracked handles** (e.g. `Player.onScreenDisplay`)
  no longer make the parent handle itself prevalidated. Previously, branding
  `onScreenDisplay` incorrectly treated plain `Player` parameters as already
  valid and silenced `missingIsValidCheck` on them.
- Add `typeIsTrackedHandle` and teach `typeOrMembersHavePrevalidatedBrand` to
  skip member-walk for tracked handle types (event payloads like
  `{ player: ValidPlayer }` still brand via members).

### Tests / docs

- Cover branded `onScreenDisplay` sync use and flag unnecessary
  `onScreenDisplay.isValid` checks.
- Document the `onScreenDisplay` branding contract in
  `require-is-valid-check` docs and `AGENTS.md`.

### Upgrade notes

After bumping, remove redundant `player.onScreenDisplay.isValid` guards when
the player is already known-valid (`ValidPlayer` or a prior `player.isValid`
check in the same sync stretch). Keep `player.isValid` after `await` /
deferred callbacks — only the display double-check is junk.

## 0.1.2

### `valid-types`

- Brand `getComponent('inventory')` containers as `ValidContainer` on entity /
  ender / item / block inventory components (class+interface merge cannot rewrite
  the class `.container` field alone).
- Brand fresh `ItemStack.getComponent` returns as Valid\*.
- Expand `ValidCallbackValue` coverage for inventory / item component returns.
- `exports["./valid-types"]` now includes a `default` condition (types-only
  exports break some resolvers).

### `no-unnecessary-is-valid-check`

- Treat bindings as known-valid when control-flow narrowing (e.g.
  `entity instanceof Player`) drops the optional Valid\* brand from the use-site
  type but the binding's **declared** type still carries it. Stops false
  negatives after `instanceof` on branded event entities like
  `EntityHitEntityAfterEvent.damagingEntity`.
- Do not flag `isValid` checks inside `catch` (try body may have invalidated
  the handle).

### Tests / fixtures

- Cover inventory container branding, `ItemStack.getComponent`, and
  `instanceof Player` on branded `entityHitEntity` payloads.

### Local consume (before npm publish)

```bash
# In the consumer repo .npmrc:
install-links=true

# package.json:
"eslint-plugin-minecraft-isvalid": "file:../eslint-plugin-minecraft-isvalid"

npm install
```

`install-links` packs `file:` deps into `node_modules` instead of symlinking.
Symlinks make `valid-types.d.ts` resolve `@minecraft/server` from the plugin
realpath (misses the consumer's install) and drop all Valid\* augmentations.
